review_response_tasks.stem: Ada often misses words in recorded conversations. She wants to hear a short part several times and read what was said after trying to understand it.
options: A

StoryTrack offers short stories in several levels. You can read one page at a time and tap an unfamiliar word for a simple meaning. There are questions after each story, but this tool does not provide spoken conversations or correct your writing.
B

SpeakPair gives you everyday situations to talk about. You record a short answer, listen to it and try again. Its main aim is to get you speaking. It is not a spelling checker, and the activities are not a collection of storybooks.
C

ListenReplay contains short recorded dialogues. You can slow a dialogue down, replay one part and then check the written script. It is useful when you want to hear where one word ends and the next begins, rather than practise writing a long text.
D

WriteFix helps you look again at your own written sentences. It marks possible spelling mistakes and explains them with examples. You decide whether to make each change. It does not offer audio stories or let you practise a conversation with a partner.
